title: Operator SLI Storyboard and Query-Cost Experimentation Notes
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a lightweight operator-facing SLI storyboard and an experimentation plan to understand query cost vs. investigation fidelity. Goal: deliver a compact dashboard + tracing anchors that help oncall identify a probable root cause within 3 drill steps while bounding query/trace cost to a target budget.

Context and motivation
- We get repeated incidents where token-latency spikes are visible in high-percentile panels but operators spend >30 minutes iterating expensive ad-hoc queries and traces.
- Tracing and session replay are powerful but query cost (and trace storage) is nontrivial for high-throughput tenants. We need a measured tradeoff: faster ROI for operators with predictable cost.

High-level story (operator journey)
1) Alarm: 99.9p latency for model-search route increases past SLO threshold.
2) First glance: compact microdash shows latency slices by stage (frontend, routing, kv-cache, model-inference) and tenant-weighted token-cost.
3) If kv-cache is hot: operator pins to "Cold-cache cohort" card to check cold-start ratio and KV miss rate.
4) If model inference stage is dominant: operator triggers a lightweight span-sample (+100 spans across random sessions) and a targeted token-sample probe for the prevailing sequence-length bucket.
5) Root cause annotated to incident ticket and follow-up: config tweak (batch size, cache TTL), model variant rollback, or capacity reallocation.

Core SLIs (proposed definitions)
- user_perceived_latency_p50/p95/p99: end-to-end from public API ingress to final response sent. Unit: ms. Aggregation: percentile over 5m windows. Tags: tenant_id, route, model_version, seq_len_bucket.
- stage_latency.kv_cache_p99: p99 of KV GET latency for requests used in inference. Unit: ms. Aggregation: per-instance and per-tenant 1m rolling.
- inference_compute_ms.p99: p99 of pure GPU compute time (kernel start->kernel end) per request. Unit: ms.
- kv_miss_ratio: fraction of requests that required remote KV load vs cache hit. Unit: ratio. Buckets: tenant, model, route.
- token_cost_rate: aggregate token_count * cost_per_token variant (derived metric) per minute. Helps correlate dollar impact.
- investigation_cost_estimate: estimated query/trace cost consumed by an operator investigation window (derived, see estimator below).

Metric contracts (short form)
- user_perceived_latency: must be computed from synchronized ingest/end timestamps; if clock skew > 200ms then mark as degraded data.
- kv_miss_ratio: require >95% sampling of requests for stability; if under-sampled, display a warning badge.
- token_cost_rate: map model_version -> per-token-rate table maintained in config repo (telemetry/cost-map).

Tracing anchors and span attributes
- Mandatory span attributes on all inference spans: tenant_id, route, model_version, seq_len_bucket, kv_key_hash_prefix (first 8 chars), cache_hit (true/false), gpu_chip_id, batch_size, kv_latency_ms.
- Suggested span name convention: inference.request -> inference.kv_lookup -> inference.model.exec -> inference.postprocess.
- Span sampling policy (proposal): dynamic, tiered strategy:
  - Always keep 1 deterministic span for first request of each high-traffic route per minute (trace_id deterministic by tenant+route+minute).
  - Adaptive reservoir: collect 250 spans per minute globally; allocate proportionally across tenants by recent error-weighted traffic (50% of reservoir) and by latency tail (50%).
  - On alarm, temporarily increase reservoir for the impacted route by factor 3 for 10 minutes.

Dashboard wireframe and microdash composition (operator-first)
- Top row (incident triage): compact SLO sparkline (p99), alarm context (last alerting rule), tenant selector, quick filter for route/model.
- Row 2: stage split stacked bar (percent latency contributed by: frontend, routing, kv-cache, model), and a correlated token_cost_rate small-panel.
- Row 3: cohort grid (small cards): cold-cache cohort, long-seq cohort, high-batch cohort. Each card shows p95 latency, kv_miss_ratio, and a one-click span-sample trigger.
- Row 4 (investigation controls): span-sample budget slider (0-500 spans), probe-run button (runs synthetic request in canary region), and estimated investigation_cost_estimate.
- Drill flow: clicking a cohort opens a session table (limit 100 rows) with link-to-trace and prompt-replay snippets (first 256 chars).

Query cost estimator (simple model)
- Inputs: approximate per-query cost (Q) = base_query_cost + per_trace_cost * traces_requested + per_rows_scanned * rows. Use conservative defaults: base_query_cost=0.005 USD, per_trace_cost=0.02 USD, per_rows_scanned=0.0001 USD.
- Example: 200 traces + 500 rows -> Q = 0.005 + 200*0.02 + 500*0.0001 = 4.005 USD. Show this as a pre-flight warning.

Experiment plan (A/B lightweight)
- Hypothesis: limiting session table rows to 100 + adaptive reservoir tracing reduces operator query cost by 60% while retaining >85% of successful root-cause captures in postmortems.
- Variants:
  - Control: current behavior (unbounded session query + trace on demand).
  - Variant A: microdash + cohort-first flow + 250 global trace reservoir.
  - Variant B: Variant A + enforced session table limit 100 and preflight cost estimation confirmation.
- Metrics to collect during experiment: investigation_cost_estimate per incident, time_to_rca (time to first actionable RCA), operator_satisfaction (survey), false_negatives (missed root cause later found in postmortem).
- Duration: 6 weeks, roll 10% -> 50% -> 100% tenants by Canary. Stop conditions: an increase >10% in mean time to RCA or HA (high-severity incident) regression.

Operator runbook (compact)
- Step 0: confirm alert and tenant. Check token_cost_rate to assess dollar urgency.
- Step 1: open microdash, look at stage split. If kv-cache >40% of latency and kv_miss_ratio>0.3, pin cold-cache cohort.
- Step 2: if model stage dominates, trigger span-sample budget 100 and run probe. Collect traces; look for increased batch_size or kernel queuing.
- Step 3: capture minimal evidence (2-3 spans + 1 probe) and annotate incident with suspected cause + proposed short-term mitigation (scale/downgrade/model pin).

Acceptance criteria for rollout
- Dashboard renders within 2s for operator with 1s p50 queries for micro-panels.
- Preflight estimation prevents >80% of investigations that would have cost >5 USD without explicit confirmation.
- Postmortem capture rate: >=85% of incidents resolved with microdash evidence vs control.

Open questions and TODOs
- Where to persist the per-token cost table (config repo vs. billing service)? Need owner.
- Exact reservoir sizing: run offline sim with last 90 days trace traffic to tune 250 global reservoir.
- UX: confirm whether sequence snippet length of 256 chars is sufficient for operators.

Notes and references
- Related issues: OBSV-482 (storyboard ticket), OBSV-515 (trace-cost-billing).
- Experiment tracking doc: linear:OBSV-482.
- Prototype PR: telemetry/pull/312 contains sample derived metrics and preflight estimator logic.

Author notes (quick)
- This is intentionally operator-facing and pragmatic: prefer smaller number of high-signal panels and automated preflight cost warnings rather than yet another large investigatory dashboard.
- Next step: prototype microdash (static) + run Canary A/B for two weeks on non-critical tenants.
